metadata.title: Payrolls Surge 162,000 in August, Tripling Forecasts

content.text:
BREAKING NEWS
Our analysts just identified a stock with the potential to be the next Nvidia. Tell us how you invest and we'll show you why it's our #1 pick. Tap here.
Everybody spent Thursday celebrating the idea of a conditional hold by the FOMC this month. Friday morning, the Bureau of Labor Statistics set that party on fire.
August payrolls came in at 162,000. Economists had penciled in 53,000. That is not so much a beat as the entire economic forecasting profession getting caught with its pants around its ankles. It's also the strongest month since March. Unemployment held at 4.1%, which is exactly where it was supposed to.
Then there were the revisions. June and July got handed a net 55,000 jobs that nobody counted the first time. The summer slowdown everybody built their September thesis around partially never happened?
One stock. Nvidia-level potential. 30M+ investors trust Moby to find it first. Get the pick. Tap here.
Wages went the wrong way too, if you love cheaper money. Hourly earnings rose 0.3% after an upwardly revised 0.2% in July, putting the annual rate at 3.1%. That's still behind inflation, with next week's CPI expected at 3.4%, so nobody's getting richer. It's just enough heat to make Christopher Waller's "Give disinflation a chance" look shakier than it did 12 hours ago.
One number deserves a squint. Food services and drinking places added 59,000 jobs against a 12-month average of 12,000. Restaurants and bars do not hire 5 times their normal pace in a single August without something odd going on in the seasonal adjustment.
The S&P and Dow sold off premarket while traders repriced the likelihood of a September rate hike that now seems inevitable from a data perspective.
